title: Window compaction: latency-bounded slice merging for fair prefill/decode throughput
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We observe tail-latency amplification for short-lived low-token requests when the scheduler aggressively splits prefill/decode into many tiny slices. This increases fairness variance (short requests starve) and raises per-token costs due to kernel switching overheads. Goal: implement a window compaction strategy that merges adjacent micro-slices within a latency budget to reduce kernel churn and improve fairness without blowing up P50/P95 targets.

Proposal:
1) Introduce a sliding 'compaction window' per GPU serving queue. Incoming prefill/decode phases are tentatively split as usual, but slices within the same window are candidate-merged if the merge keeps the combined expected latency under the request's latency budget.
2) Estimator: use lightweight kernel cost model (informed by prior kernel probe metrics) to predict merged slice cost. Apply conservative headroom multiplier for new/unknown models.
3) Fairness admission: track per-customer short-request credit; if a merge would push short-request credits negative, do not compact for that window.
4) Hedged fastpath: for latency-sensitive requests (marked by route or SLA), allow a fastpath that bypasses compaction and hedges into a dedicated small-slot queue.
5) Fallback and telemetry: if compaction causes regression for a workload, automatically reduce compaction window length for that route via feedback from the quality and latency monitors.

Acceptance criteria:
- p50 token latency on representative short-request workload: <= baseline + 5ms
- p95 latency improvement of >= 10% on mixed workloads dominated by short requests and intermittent long prefill jobs
- Kernel switch count per 1M tokens reduced by >= 15% in benchmarks
- No regression on customer-facing integration tests or model fidelity alerts

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-route percentage rollout (start at 1%).
- Canary on internal staging with synthetic mixed workloads (short-burst + long fills).
- Observe for 72h, then increase to 10% for 48h, then 50% and full roll when stable.

Notes: This approach prioritizes reducing kernel churn and improving short-request fairness while preserving throughput for long prefill workloads. It complements existing phase-splitting policies by adding an optimizer that can un-split when helpful.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after analyzing recent perf spikes in us-east-1 staging. Attached initial perf plots and incident notes in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-window-compaction-spike

2026-03-03 - Jordan Lee: Completed small spike to instrument kernel probe costs per slice; results show median kernel setup overhead ~2.1ms, 95th ~6.3ms for models in runtime-1.20 baseline. Saved probe data to metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/serving/kernel-costs

2026-03-04 - Priya Menon (review): Suggest adding per-model conservative multiplier for unknown quantized kernels to avoid underestimation. Also asked for test harness for corner case where merge increases KV-cache misses.

2026-03-06 - Jordan Lee: Implemented prototype compaction window in sandbox branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/7892. Prototype contains: window policy, estimator stub, and fairness credits. Perf run (mixed synthetic) shows kernel switches down 18% and p95 latency down 12% for short requests.

2026-03-08 - QA: Ran integration tests with heavy burst traffic and long prefill jobs. Observed one regression: a model with dynamic attention tiling experienced increased latency after compaction due to cache-eviction interactions. Added a heuristic to disable compaction for models flagged by kernel-probe as 'cache-sensitive'.
2026-03-09 - Security: Confirmed no new data path changes; feature flagged. No security review required at prototyping stage.

2026-03-10 - Jordan Lee: Updated estimator to include kernel affinity hint (from ENG-51674). Preparing canary config and will enable at 1% for runtime-1.22 staging tomorrow. Next steps: add rollout dashboards, automate feedback loop to shrink window on regressions, and add a small suite of fuzz tests to catch cache-sensitivity regressions.
